steps.label: Why Do We Need to Search?
steps.content:
Why Do We Need to Search?

You already know how to loop through every value in an array. A search uses exactly that loop, but compares each value with something instead of adding it up.

  • A linear search checks one item at a time, starting from the first position.
  • It compares each item with the value being searched for.
  • It keeps checking until every item has been compared.
  • A linear search works on any list, even one that is not sorted.

Practise Tracing an Array

Before writing your own search, practise following a loop that works through an array one item at a time.

Steps

  2. At the top of the page, select Cambridge pseudocode.
  3. Open Walkthrough and choose Array Iteration.
  4. Predict what the program will output before pressing Step Forward.

steps.label: Write It Yourself
steps.content:
Write It Yourself

Use the same structure you just learned, but write it yourself this time.

Task

The array Ages = [15, 22, 8, 34, 19] is already stored, five values. Write pseudocode that:

  • asks for a SearchAge
  • searches every value in Ages
  • outputs "Found" or "Not Found"

Remember

  • Set Found <- FALSE before the loop.
  • Use FOR Index <- 1 TO 5 to check every position.
  • Inside the loop, only ever set Found to TRUE, never back to FALSE.
  • Test Found in a second IF, after NEXT Index.

steps.label: Check Your Understanding
steps.content:
Check Your Understanding

Questions to ask around the room:

  • What does a linear search check first?
  • What does the FOR loop count through?
  • Why do we need a Found flag?
  • Does the search stop as soon as it finds a match?
  • What happens if the value is not in the array?

steps.label: Plenary: Question 1
steps.content:
Plenary

Use everything from today. Try this on your own before checking your answer.

Task

The array Colours = ["Red", "Green", "Blue", "Yellow"] is already stored, four values. Write pseudocode that:

  • asks for a SearchColour
  • searches every value in Colours
  • outputs "Found" or "Not Found"

Remember

  • Set Found <- FALSE before the loop.
  • Colours has four values, so the loop must count from 1 to 4.
  • Test Found in a second IF, after NEXT Index.

steps.label: Plenary: Question 2
steps.content:
Plenary

Harder than Question 1, a bigger array with the match at the very last position.

Task

The array Names = ["Ivy", "Omar", "Zara", "Leo", "Mia", "Kofi"] is already stored, six values. Write pseudocode that:

  • asks for a SearchName
  • searches every value in Names
  • outputs "Found" or "Not Found"

Remember

  • Set Found <- FALSE before the loop.
  • Names has six values, so the loop must count from 1 to 6.
  • The loop still checks every position, even after it finds a match.
